note: disposition: bound (confirmed against the implementation) | approximated (maps with stated loss) | unsupported (declared, with stated behaviour) | unverified (coverage detected, mapping not yet confirmed by a human). Only bound rows are claims; unverified rows are work.

rotation.notes: Emits `transform: rotate(<n>deg)`. A rotation of 0 is suppressed because it matches the CSS initial value and a transform would otherwise create a containing block for absolute descendants.

visible.notes: Only `false` emits, as `display: none`. A visible element says nothing, so the display its layout chose is not overridden. A variant revealing an element hidden in the default restores display from the default element's own layout mode.

opacity.notes: A literal ratio is emitted directly. A token is multiplied into a percentage — `calc(<var> * 1%)` — because an opacity variable is authored on a 0–100 scale.

locked.notes: Not emitted. `locked` is a canvas-interaction concept with no CSS counterpart, and the transform has no awareness of the key. The value is dropped with no warning.

backgroundColor.notes: Emits `background`. A gradient resolves to a CSS gradient function; a `null` becomes `transparent`. Loss: a gradient stop whose position is not a number silently becomes 0, and a gradient with fewer than two resolvable stops is dropped entirely rather than degraded.

backgroundImage.notes: Emitted from the sheet layer, outside the main style pipeline. `background-position`, `background-repeat` and `background-size` are emitted independently of whether the image reference resolves — deliberately, so the fit behaviour is conveyed regardless. `objectFit: CONTAIN` becomes `background-size: contain`; everything else, including absent, becomes `cover`. Loss: the source path is reduced to its basename, discarding any directory structure.

fillColor.notes: The CSS property depends on the element type: a glyph or vector takes `background-color`, an untyped legacy element takes `fill`, anything else takes `background`. Loss: a gradient fill on an untyped element is skipped entirely, because an inline SVG paint has no gradient equivalent.

textColor.notes: Emits `color`. A gradient becomes a four-declaration bundle — background, both background-clip prefixes, and a transparent colour — which is the standard way to paint text with a gradient.

effects.notes: Emits `box-shadow`, `filter` and `backdrop-filter`. A `null` resets all three. Loss: a shadow whose offset, blur or spread cannot be resolved substitutes `0`, and an unresolvable colour substitutes `currentColor`, so an unresolved value is masked as a plausible one rather than reported. A blur whose radius fails to resolve emits nothing at all and no reset.

clipsContent.notes: Emits `overflow: hidden` or `overflow: visible`. A non-boolean is dropped.

cornerRadius.notes: Emits `border-radius`, reordering a per-corner object from the schema's logical order into CSS's. Loss: a corner that cannot be resolved substitutes `0` rather than being reported, and an unresolved token radius with no cached fallback degrades to the keyword `unset`. An ellipse receives `border-radius: 50%` only when this key produced nothing.

minWidth.notes: Emits `min-width`. Loss: a resolved value of `0` is suppressed, so an explicit zero minimum is indistinguishable from an unstated one.

minHeight.notes: Emits `min-height`, with the same zero suppression as `minWidth`. Unlike `height`, it is not suppressed when an aspect ratio is stated.

maxWidth.notes: Emits `max-width`. Loss: a resolved value of `0` is suppressed — and unlike a minimum, a maximum of zero is a constraint the schema permits and Figma accepts, so this one is a CSS-side choice rather than a platform limit.

maxHeight.notes: Emits `max-height`, with the same zero suppression as `maxWidth`.

strokeDashPattern.notes: Not emitted. CSS offers no control over border dash geometry — `border-style: dashed` exists but its dash and gap lengths are chosen by the user agent — so the schema's explicit `{ dash, gap }` in pixels cannot be honoured. A dashed stroke currently renders solid, because the border style the transform emits is always `solid`.

typography.notes: A resolvable token emits the `font` shorthand plus a companion `letter-spacing`, since the shorthand cannot carry tracking. Otherwise each member emits its own property, and `fontStyle` is split into `font-weight` and `font-style`. Loss: a weight word absent from the recognised map loses `font-weight` while italic detection still succeeds; `textCase` and `textDecoration` values outside their maps are dropped silently; and the companion letter-spacing depends on a pattern match against the resolved variable name, which if it fails loses tracking.

textAlignHorizontal.notes: Remaps the schema's logical values to CSS logical keywords: `START` to `start`, `END` to `end`, `JUSTIFY` to `justify`. All four schema values are covered, so the fallback is unreachable for valid input.

textAlignVertical.notes: Not emitted for an element's `styles`. The key is absent from the style pipeline entirely, so a plain element carrying it produces nothing. The separate `contentStyles` member of the same name IS handled for a text primitive filling a slot, and only where that slot admits no components — two different members with one name, and only one of them is realised.

primaryAxisSizingMode.notes: Not emitted. Sizing is derived instead from `layoutSizingHorizontal` and `layoutSizingVertical` against the parent axis, which the `autoLayoutSizing` cluster states. This key is never read.

itemReverseZIndex.notes: The key is never read. The semantic it names is approximated by a different mechanism: a variant whose layout reverses the default's child order emits `row-reverse` or `column-reverse`, derived from comparing the two layout trees. A partial reorder is not expressible that way and is handled by relocating the element instead.

padding.notes: A uniform value emits `padding`; a `null` emits `padding: 0`. A per-side object emits a `padding-block` and `padding-inline` pair, deliberately avoiding the four-value shorthand so a logical side is never misread as a physical one — the direction-safe treatment Figma lacks. Defect: a side present but unresolvable is omitted with no fallback, while `cornerRadius` substitutes `0` for the same class of failure. Nothing should be dropped; the two disagree.

cornerSmoothing.notes: Not emitted, and nothing attempts a substitute. CSS has no squircle primitive; a clip-path or mask approximation would change the element's box rather than its corner, so none is offered.

autoLayout.notes: css/style/layoutToCSS.ts:39-96; css/sheet/elementRules.ts:254-268. `cases` decides display and direction; `memberCases` apply only when a case above emitted a display.

cases.why: without a layout mode the whole cluster is inert; the element stays in flow

emit: NOT on this element — a negative margin on `<selector> > * + *`, emitted by elementRules
memberCases.why: gap does not accept negative values; overlap is a sibling margin

autoLayoutSizing.notes: css/style/layoutToCSS.ts:130-179. Cases are ordered and the first match wins. `self.layoutSizingOnParentAxis` is the axis-selected key the source computes from parentLayoutMode.

cases.why: the parent main axis already hugs
the parent stretches it across the cross axis already
stated sizing on a flex child that is not FILL must not shrink

otherwise.why: FIXED or absent contributes nothing from this cluster

absolutePositioning.notes: css/style/position.ts:4-27 (hasInsets, impliesAbsolute), 42-59, 84-107 (centerDecls). `cases` decides the position property; `insetCases` decides the offsets. verticalAnchored/horizontalAnchored are presence of top|bottom and start|end respectively.

cases.why: no coordinates, nothing to infer from
outside auto-layout, any coordinate is meaningful
inside auto-layout only a meaningful coordinate implies absolute
a zero-only single anchor inside auto-layout is canvas noise

insetCases.why: an edge anchor on the same axis wins; both would put two values on one property

emit: translate: <-50% on each centred axis, 0 on the other>

strokeRendering.notes: css/style/border.ts:51-53, 73-167. strokeAlign contributes no declaration of its own — it only flips the outline-offset sign. `strokeDashPattern` is NOT consulted: see its own row.

asOutline.source: border.ts:51-53 — a per-side object becomes border-*, a scalar or token becomes outline-*

cases.why: a gradient stroke is painted by a separate pseudo-element rule, not a border or outline

emit: border-width: 0 or outline-width: 0, matching whichever style was emitted
cases.why: a default block must reset a width it did not state

intrinsicSize.notes: css/style/size.ts:22-34. minWidth, minHeight, maxWidth and maxHeight are independent and map one-to-one.

cases.why: a stated ratio derives the height

textTruncation.notes: css/style/truncation.ts:12-37. The multi-line case sets display, so it interacts with the autoLayout cluster on the same element.

cases.why: multi-line clamp changes the display type

valueForms.summary: Every style value may be a literal, a TokenReference, a PropBinding, or a Conditional. A disposition for a key means little without saying what happens to each form (DSPEC-42).
valueForms.literalNote: The ordinary case; every case table above is written against literals.
valueForms.tokenReferenceNote: Emitted per `settings.spec.tokens`. A dedicated token-value path recognises `$token` and renders it in the configured notation.
valueForms.propBindingNote: A PropBinding is not applied to any style value. `visible` is the one possible exception and is not currently realised either: the check is a literal `false` comparison, which a `{ $binding }` object fails, so a bound visibility emits nothing. Declared scope, not an unfound gap.
valueForms.conditionalNote: Not yet implemented. Nothing in the transform matches a conditional, so a `visible` carrying the ADR-018 conditional form renders permanently visible and the condition is discarded. The render path does implement it, so a document survives a Figma round trip and loses the condition only on the way to CSS.

realises: The style surface. Every output in this binding is a CSS declaration, so it is shared by every platform that styles with CSS rather than belonging to any one of them.

onAbsentVocabulary.declaredDefault: Applies the value the schema declares for an absent key.
onAbsentVocabulary.platformInitial: Applies the platform's own initial value, which may differ from the schema's declared default.
onAbsentVocabulary.unverified: Nobody has established what this platform does when the key is absent.

onAbsentNote: What this platform does when a style key is absent from a document. The schema declares the meaning of absence once (§4.1a); this records whether the platform honours it. A row whose onAbsent is not declaredDefault is a disagreement with the contract, and each one is a decision rather than an accident.

basisVocabulary.implementation: Verified against a citable implementation. The drift guard checks it, and a change to that implementation fails the build.
basisVocabulary.intent: Asserted from the authoritative source for what the data means, which is not publicly citable. Nothing mechanical checks it; a reviewer must.

basisNote: Every claim here is verified against a citable implementation in this repository.

colorSpace.title: A non-sRGB ColorObject renders as if it were sRGB
colorSpace.note: The schema admits 14 colour spaces and the render path never reads `colorSpace` — components 0 through 2 are taken as red, green and blue regardless, so an `oklch` value is misread rather than approximated. A `none` component becomes 0, and components beyond the third are dropped.
colorSpace.decided: Convert to sRGB at render time (#813). The schema keeps all 14 spaces; the render path gains a conversion with gamut mapping for values outside sRGB. Until that lands, a non-sRGB ColorObject renders wrong rather than degraded.

explicitZero.title: Zero is not distinguishable from unset
explicitZero.note: Both platforms currently treat a dimension of 0 as "no constraint" rather than "a constraint of zero".
explicitZero.decided: Open. Deferred — see #814, and #812 on what an absent `width`/`height` means. The two interact and should be settled together.

logicalToPhysical.title: Logical sides become physical without a direction
logicalToPhysical.note: The schema uses `start` and `end` so a document is direction-agnostic. The Figma render maps `start` to the left padding with no writing-direction branch.
logicalToPhysical.decided: Accepted as a platform limit. Figma cannot express a writing direction, so the mapping is left-to-right only and the loss is declared rather than fixed — which is what `approximated` means. CSS stays direction-safe by emitting `padding-block` and `padding-inline`.

partialOnUnresolved.title: A value is dropped rather than degraded
partialOnUnresolved.note: A gradient whose stops do not yield two resolvable colours is dropped whole. A `padding` side that is present but unresolvable is omitted while its siblings emit, whereas `cornerRadius` substitutes `0` for the same failure. DSPEC-43 says a degradation applies the spec's own recorded fallback, or applies nothing and warns — dropping part of a value silently is neither.
partialOnUnresolved.decided: Open. See #816 on the disagreement between the composite types, and #815 on the gradient path.
